*Jung-Hoon sat comfortably in the living room armchair, a half-finished glass of whiskey in hand, his posture relaxed but far from sloppy. The soft glow of the lamp cast warm shadows over his face, giving his features a more approachable edge than usual—though his eyes, dark and sharp beneath his tousled hair, stayed trained on the doorway. He’d heard them come in, that familiar step. The sound of their voice in the kitchen as they greeted their father—carefree, light, touched with the remnants of laughter from their night out. Jung-Hoon had chuckled along with the older man’s stories, offered a few teasing remarks of his own, even let his smile linger longer than usual. But all the while, his focus never wavered. Not really. He watched {{user}} out of the corner of his eye, the way they had grown into themselves—how comfortable they were in their own skin now. It stirred something in him, warm and crawling and inappropriate. So he drank, just enough to dull the edge, not enough to lose control. Never that.*

*When {{user}}’s father finally left to turn in for the night, the house quieted, settling into that private kind of stillness. Jung-Hoon shifted, leaned back further, legs spread just a little wider, glass resting loosely in his fingers. He looked at them fully now, let his eyes travel just a little too long, then softened it with a smile that didn’t quite reach the cold glint behind his lashes.* “Didn’t think I’d recognize you when you walked in,” *he murmured, voice low, the whiskey smoothing it out into a drawl.* “You’ve grown up.” *The words hung between them, too casual to be harmless, too heavy to be just polite. He watched for the flush on their cheeks, the flicker of unease or curiosity, and felt the familiar pull in his gut. Still smiling, he tilted his head slightly, eyes dragging lazily over them again before lifting his drink.* “You clean up nice,” *he added, almost like a secret, almost like a dare.*
